text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear position that driverless cars will \"greatly decrease the amount of accidents\"","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a direct, easy-to-follow claim early and keeps the reader oriented to the writer's stance."},{"evidence":"paragraphs on lower accidents, cheaper fuel, and less greenhouse gases","quality":"organized support","description":"It develops the argument in separate points instead of piling ideas together in one vague stream."},{"evidence":"mentions LIDAR, GPS, radar, and antilock brakes","quality":"specific evidence use","description":"It uses concrete details from the article to explain why the cars could work and why they may be safer."},{"evidence":"explains sensors alert the driver when they cannot handle a situation","quality":"reasoned explanation","description":"It does more than name facts by showing how the technology connects to the claim that the cars are useful."},{"evidence":"opening, body paragraphs, and a concluding restatement","quality":"essay structure","description":"It has a recognizable introduction, middle, and conclusion that make the argument feel complete."},{"evidence":"fewer distracting errors than B","quality":"sentence control","description":"Its wording is still weak, but it is more readable and less derailed by grammar and word-choice problems than the other essay."}]}
